description: Replace the n2048 eight-rank reducer's full-reflector replication barrier with a chunked producer-consumer pipeline: deliver coalesced reflector stripes through TMA multicast or a multi-source DSM tree, use mbarriers so all nineteen A*v warps begin on completed stripes, double-buffer panel state across groups, and retain GPU-wide tensor-core trailing updates, exact reflector ownership, certificates, fallbacks, other size routes, and CUDA guards.

Initial 256-float DSM stripe pipeline reached NVCC but failed because this parent no longer included the stock cuda/ptx wrappers or namespace alias used by the prior bulk-copy branch. No metric or commit was produced; the next trial adds only that required stock header wiring.

Replaced n2048 scalar full-reflector pulls with eight 256-float shared-to-cluster bulk-copy stripes, one local mbarrier per stripe/rank, and register-resident four-row raw A*v sums. Rank-0 projection runs concurrently with remote stripe waits; all 19 CTA warps consume each completed stripe, exact inner order and GPU-wide baddbmm updates remain intact. Stock PTX build and kernelguard pass; validation is 39/39. Metric is 31423.823 and n2048 is 93828.139 us versus the parent near 84000 us, showing eight CTA barriers plus 56 bulk-copy launches per reflector outweigh overlap.

Changed each remote 256-float stripe handoff from one CTA leader wait plus __syncthreads to one mbarrier acquire per warp leader plus __syncwarp, so all 19 A*v warps begin independently while keeping the same transfer topology and arithmetic. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric improves trial 1 from 31423.823 to 31349.359 and n2048 from 93828.139 to 91882.060 us, but remains far behind the parent near 84000 us; CTA barriers were costly but 56 TMA instructions and eight phases still dominate.

Coarsened the warp-acquired n2048 producer-consumer pipeline from eight 256-float stripes to four 512-float stripes, halving mbarrier phases and shared-to-cluster bulk copies from 56 to 28 per reflector while retaining early warp starts and exact-order sums. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric is 31316.212; n2048 improves from 91882.060 to 90315.241 us but is still about 6.3 ms behind parent, confirming launch/phase overhead dominates any fine-stripe overlap.

Coarsened the DSM pipeline again to two 1024-float phases and 14 bulk copies per full reflector. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, but metric regresses to 31408.744 and n2048 to 93190.363 us from the four-phase 90315.241 us. The 4 KiB transfers lose more than the reduced synchronization saves, bounding the best bulk-copy granularity at 512 floats in this topology.

Replaced rank-0 fanout with a multi-source DSM tree at the best 512-float granularity: rank 0 seeds ranks 1/2/4, then ranks 2/4/6 forward to 3/5+6/7 after their stripe mbarrier completes, leaving 18 warps per forwarding CTA free for A*v. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, including the deepest forwarding rank. Metric regresses to 31410.225 and n2048 to 94294.533 us versus direct fanout 90315.241; serialized tree depth and forwarding-warp issue cost exceed rank-0 issue serialization.

Replaced four 512-float point-to-point fanouts with four global-stage TMA cluster multicasts. Distributed normalization writes the existing values workspace, rank 0 issues one masked multicast per stripe, and each remote warp acquires its local stripe mbarrier before exact-order A*v accumulation. Compiles for sm_100a with stock PTX wrappers; kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric is 31282.795 and n2048 is 90186.681 us, statistically similar to direct fanout 90315.241 despite reducing 28 copy instructions to four; global staging and four-phase register-resident dot overhead dominate.

Profile-guided in-place multicast variant removed four live row accumulators: every warp streams stripe completions only into its first row slot, publishes rank-0 projection scalars after that slot, then processes remaining resident-vector rows sequentially; panel column 0 skips the unneeded cluster barrier and non-n2048 routes regain their original one-sum schedule. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric is 31266.060 and n2048 is 89888.852 us versus 90186.681 for four live sums. NCU on the predecessor showed 96 versus parent 90 registers and about 9% extra instructions, so the small recovery confirms bookkeeping remains costly.

Coarsened the one-accumulator TMA multicast pipeline from four 512-float phases to two 1024-float phases, halving warp acquires and multicast instructions. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric is 31268.096 and n2048 is 90277.748 us versus four-phase 89888.852 us; even without point-to-point fanout, 4 KiB phases lose about 0.39 ms, so 512-float stripes remain the best chunked configuration.

Collapsed the in-place multicast route to one full 2048-float transfer as a no-early-start control. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, but metric regresses to 31347.096 and n2048 to 94808.421 us. Having all 19 warp leaders contend on one 8 KiB mbarrier is much worse than the historical single-CTA-wait full multicast, while that historical route was already slower than the parent; the useful chunked endpoint remains four 512-float phases.

Corrected the pipeline's scope after detecting that the generalized compile-time row mapping used launch bounds rather than n352's actual 384-thread CTA. Restored the original runtime projection and A*v row loops exactly for n352/n1024, retained only the profiled n2048 one-accumulator four-by-512 TMA multicast path, and restored the n352 fast route from 25.2 ms fallback behavior to 4.734 ms. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass with the original n352 trajectory. Clean aggregate metric is 27447.341 versus parent final 27313.233; n2048 remains 89970.973 us versus parent near 84000 us, so the chunked path is a measured regression despite preserving all other routes.

Optimized the clean four-by-512 multicast route so only each dot group's first row streams stripe phases and overlaps rank-0 projection; after that row publishes projection scalars, remaining rows use the parent's direct inner loop over the now-resident local reflector instead of re-entering all four stripe loops. Other sizes remain original. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. n2048 improves from 89970.973 to 87494.156 us and clean metric from 27447.341 to 27385.557, leaving about 2.1 ms n2048 and 72 us aggregate behind parent final 27313.233.

Reduced remote mbarrier polling from 19 warp leaders to one CTA leader per stripe; the leader publishes completion through a fenced shared ready flag and each warp leader spins locally before __syncwarp, avoiding a block barrier. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass, but n2048 regresses from 87494.156 to 87694.537 us and metric to 27403.945. Shared flag polling and the producer warp's serialized wait cost slightly more than direct per-warp mbarrier acquires.

Restored direct per-warp mbarrier acquisition and retested eight 256-float multicast stripes after limiting phased bookkeeping to the first row only. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. n2048 is 87496.938 us, statistically identical to the four-by-512 result 87494.156 us; aggregate 27377.420 versus 27385.557 reflects unrelated shape noise. Earlier reflector availability exactly offsets four additional multicast/acquire phases, so 512 remains the simpler best-equivalent pipeline.

Restored the parent reducer after exhausting chunked variants and applied a four-line in-place overlap: for panel columns 1-10, remote CTAs perform the existing scalar full-reflector replication while rank 0 computes projection scalars, then the existing cluster.sync publishes both; only column 0 retains the separate CTA barrier. This removes ten redundant __syncthreads per full panel without changing ownership, arithmetic, GPU-wide baddbmm updates, routes, guards, or shared footprint. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. n2048 is 84162.654 us versus the best chunked 87494.156; aggregate 27301.160 slightly improves parent final 27313.233 and is near parent replay 27299.360.

Refined the scalar in-place fallback to preserve each remote CTA's original __syncthreads copy-completion barrier while rank 0 skips its empty local barrier and proceeds directly to projection/A*v; later cluster synchronization and partial-dot synchronization retain all cross-rank ordering. Kernelguard and 39/39 validation pass. Metric is 27314.005 and n2048 is 84140.773 us, about 22 us faster than the combined-cluster-barrier variant and statistically neutral against parent final 27313.233; exact profiling is required for selection.

Final selection restores the exact parent source tree after paired measurements rejected every alternative. Final build and kernelguard pass; validation is 39/39. Final metric is 27320.275 with n2048 84027.194 us, consistent with parent final/replays 27313.233/27299.360 and faster than rank-0 barrier removal 84140.773, combined barrier 84162.654, best chunked multicast 87494.156, direct fanout 90315.241, and DSM tree 94294.533. Git tree for submission.py exactly matches ba5dd15a4.

Final commit 5521fecdd restores the exact ba5dd15a4 submission tree after exhaustive chunked and in-place trials; final build/kernelguard pass, validation 39/39, metric 27320.275, n2048 84027.194 us. Parent exact nsys reducer was 116.196 ms across two calls (372 launches), 70.2% of captured time; parent NCU showed 90 registers, 29.69% occupancy, 0.17-0.18 eligible warps/scheduler, and long-scoreboard dominance. Best correct chunked design used four 512-float global-stage TMA multicasts, per-rank stripe mbarriers, all 19 warp consumers, rank-0 projection overlap, and direct resident-vector loops after the first row; it reached n2048 87494.156 us and metric 27385.557, with reducer 123.219 ms. Eight 256-float stripes tied it; two/four live row sums, CTA barriers, shared ready flags, direct fanout, 4 KiB phases, one-phase warp waits, and multi-source DSM tree were slower. NCU on the four-live-sum version showed 96 registers and about 9% more executed instructions despite lower scoreboard stalls. The strongest scalar in-place variants combined copy/projection synchronization or skipped rank-0's empty copy barrier, but exact reducer totals 116.481/116.346 ms and n2048 84163/84141 us remained slower than parent 116.196 ms/84027 us. GPU-wide baddbmm updates, ownership, certificates, fallbacks, other routes, and guards were preserved throughout; no leaderboard submission was made per brief.
